components.name: Direct Entry
components.description: No-personalization browse choice: quiet until keyboard/remote focus.

narrative.overview: Wabbit TV is a calm, local-first launch board for a user-owned viewing library: near-black structure recedes so real provider artwork can carry color. It is an Operate surface for a Windows desk or couch; browsing stays organized, legible, and deliberately unpromotional.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite field, warm-white hierarchy, one precise amber signal.
Dense, shelf-led browsing rather than a hero or provider storefront.
Crisp spatial navigation with equal mouse, keyboard, and remote access.

rules.name: The Local Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal amber communicates selection, focus, and the one immediate action—not branding wallpaper. Rabbit personality is reserved for the application icon, empty/onboarding moments, and loading; the everyday shell remains restrained.

rules.name: The Artwork Boundary Rule
rules.body: Runtime provider artwork may be colorful. The geometric palettes visible in the proof are clearly synthetic local fixtures, not a product artwork system or a source of additional UI accents.

rules.name: The Shelf-Not-Hero Rule
rules.body: Context belongs beside the selected item in the first pinned shelf. It never becomes a promotional banner or reserves invented metadata when there is no item.

rules.name: The Directional Return Rule
rules.body: Left on the first content item opens the rail; Escape returns to the rail; leaving the rail restores the last viable content focus. Arrows move predictably within and between shelves, Enter/Select activates, and mouse hover never gates an action.

dos: Do preserve the Windows title bar and Segoe UI identity in this Windows-first surface.
Do use signal amber for focus, selection, and the immediate no-source action.
Do use real provider art at runtime and identify development art as fixture-only.
Do separately shape detailed cards, source setup, player controls, PiP, multiview, and non-Windows platform patterns before adding visible UI.
donts: Don't create a promotional hero, recommendation rail, provider category shelves, gradients, glass, neon bloom, or decorative blobs.
Don't treat illustrative titles, source labels, connection state, or artwork as product claims.
Don't add hover-only behavior or allow focus motion to shift the underlying content layout.
Don't generalize this Home grammar into an app-wide component library without a separately shaped need.
